mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate relative to its 12-month moving average compresses equity discount rates, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate accommodative monetary policy.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS declines by at least 0.25 percentage points over the prior 3 months, or the Rank IC falls below 0.05 over any 12-month rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 2.5% for two consecutive months, it signals a tightening cycle that increases equity discount rates, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as investors price in higher borrowing costs.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS exceeds 2.5% for two consecutive months, or the Rank IC is negative over any 6-month rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A rising unemployment rate combined with a rising federal funds rate signals an economic slowdown under tight monetary policy, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as investors anticipate reduced corporate earnings and higher risk aversion.
regime_hint: monetary tightening and labor market deterioration
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE rises > 0.2pp and FEDFUNDS rises > 0.1pp over the prior 3 months, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.03 over any 12-month window.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansions, a decline in residential construction permits below 1700 thousand units signals weakening housing demand, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate reduced consumer spending and economic growth.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when HOUST < 1700 and the economy is in a late-cycle expansion, or the Rank IC for HOUST in late-cycle is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in non-farm payroll employment above its 12-month moving average indicates a strengthening labor market, which supports consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when PAYEMS increases by at least 100,000 over the prior 3 months, or the Rank IC falls below 0.05 over any 6-month rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production falls below 100 for two consecutive months, it signals a contraction in manufacturing output, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as investors anticipate reduced corporate profits and economic slowdown.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when INDPRO < 100 for two consecutive months, or the Rank IC is negative over any 12-month rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in residential construction permits below 1700 thousand units combined with a decline in industrial production below 100 signals a simultaneous weakening in housing demand and manufacturing supply, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate a broad-based economic slowdown.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when HOUST < 1700 and INDPRO < 100, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.03 over any 12-month window.

mechanism_narrative: During monetary tightening cycles, a rising consumer price index above 5.0% annually signals persistent inflation, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as the Federal Reserve delays rate cuts and increases discount rates.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL annual rate > 5.0% and the Fed is in a tightening cycle, or the Rank IC for CPIAUCSL in tightening cycles is below 0.03.
